visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young man with black hair, wearing a black t-shirt and a silver chain, sits at a white table in a bright indoor room. He holds a white steamed bun in his right hand and makes a peace sign with his left. A pink decorative fan and various household items are visible on a counter behind him. (2) The scene cuts to the same man now wearing a blue Fubon Braves basketball jersey and a black baseball cap. He holds the bun and smiles while showing the number 'one' with his finger. (3) The video enters a montage phase, rapidly cutting between the man in the black t-shirt (Japanese persona) and the man in the blue jersey (Taiwanese persona). They compare hand gestures for numbers two through nine. The man in the black shirt expresses shock and disgust, at one point covering his mouth with his hand. (4) The man in the blue jersey takes a large bite of the bun, looking satisfied. The man in the black shirt waves his hands frantically in distress. (5) The man in the black shirt bows his head deeply onto the white table in a gesture of defeat.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) High-energy upbeat electronic BGM starts immediately. A male voice speaks in a mocking, high-pitched Japanese persona with fast speech. (2) A sharp 'Whoosh' SFX triggers as the man switches to a Mandarin persona, speaking a calm, friendly 'Yi' (one). (3) Rapid succession of 'Whoosh' SFX and comedic 'boing' sounds occur as the voices alternate. The Japanese persona lets out a loud, high-pitched gagging sound 'Bleh' in surprise. (4) Rhythmic BGM continues while the voices shout numbers in Mandarin and Japanese. A loud 'Nani!?' (What!?) is shouted with high vocal tension and arousal. (5) Audible crunching and chewing SFX play as the Taiwanese persona eats. This is contrasted by frantic, strained shouting from the Japanese persona. (6) A final 'Impact' thud SFX is heard as the man slams his head on the table, followed by a long, defeated groan 'Mairimashita' (I lost).

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: To humorously compare and contrast the different hand-counting gestures used in Japan versus Taiwan, using a two-persona skit format to highlight cultural surprises.
